Chloe / HealthCo — initial draft below. I put the short answers up top and attached a simplified trace PDF.

Quick answers:
- Data path (short): Client -> TLS terminated at regional edge (EU-west) -> request routed to EU inferencing pool -> model host loads KV prefix/cached segments from ephemeral NVMe in the same AZ -> inference response streamed back. No token-level logs are persisted outside the EU tenant unless customer opt-in to analytics.
- KV/cache residency: Ephemeral NVMe local to the instance (retention: ephemeral for session length; by default TTL < 1 hour; explicit cache persists only when customer enables long-cache feature). All ephemeral caches remain in the EU region.
- Key ownership: This tenant currently uses Redwood-managed KMS in eu-west-1. Operator roster is attached; keys are not customer-managed for this tenant.

Notes:
- If customer requires customer-managed keys (CMKs), we support Bring-Your-Own-Key via our Private offering (VPC + KMS integration). That requires a short onboarding and a support ticket for key handshake (typical lead time 5 business days).
- SOC 2 reference: see SOC2 summary (attached) — section 3.2 (encryption & key management) and 4.1 (change control) are the most relevant.
- CAIQ / SIG: I bookmarked the CAIQ matrix sheet with the relevant controls (control IDs: CR-01, KE-02, TR-03 in our internal mapping). Marissa can add exact CAIQ cell links.

I attached: residency-path-trace.pdf (1 page diagram) and a small operator CSV extract keystore-operators-2026-03.csv (3 rows: ops-team@redwood.ai, key-rotations@example, oncall).
